question: An evaluation team is assembling test cases for a clause-extraction feature used on uploaded contracts. The current dataset contains only well-formatted, standard commercial leases. Following evaluation design best practices, which addition would most improve the test set's ability to predict real-world failures?
options: A) A larger number of well-formatted standard leases, so the existing category has more statistical confidence behind its accuracy score
B) A stratified set of malformed, scanned, and non-standard contracts added alongside the standard leases to mirror production documents
C) A panel of legal experts who re-extract clauses from the existing standard leases to double-check the original human labels
D) A set of contracts translated into several languages, so multilingual fluency can be scored alongside extraction accuracy
correct_answers: B) A stratified set of malformed, scanned, and non-standard contracts added alongside the standard leases to mirror production documents
explanations: Incorrect. Adding more examples of a single, already well-represented category does not address the missing coverage of edge cases and non-standard documents, which is the actual gap.

Correct. Task-specific evaluation design calls for mirroring the real-world task distribution, including edge cases like malformed or non-standard inputs the model will actually encounter in production.
Incorrect. Re-verifying labels on the existing standard-lease examples improves label quality but does not expand the test set's coverage of the edge cases the model will face in production.

Incorrect. Multilingual fluency is a different capability than clause extraction on the documents this feature will actually process; it does not address the identified gap in document format coverage.
